![bluelineR](reference/figures/logo.png)

bluelineR wraps the public APIs behind NHL.com and returns tidy tibbles:
scores, schedules, standings, play-by-play, box scores and shift charts;
players, rosters, stat leaders and the draft; the stats and records
APIs; **NHL EDGE** skating, shot and zone-time tracking; and the **puck
and player tracking frames behind every goal since 2023-24**, ten frames
a second, with tools that read how each goal was scored and draw it on a
rink.

It grew out of [BluelineMetrics](https://bluelinemetrics.com), where
these endpoints feed the live game tracker, the goal replays and the
player pages.

![Connor McDavid's overtime winner in the 2025 4 Nations Face-Off final,
drawn from the NHL's player and puck tracking: Canada in red, the United
States in navy, Marner and Makar on the assists, and GOAL as the puck
goes in.](reference/figures/README-hero.gif)

Connor McDavid’s overtime winner in the 4 Nations final, from the NHL’s
player and puck tracking, drawn by
[`animate_goal()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/animate_goal.md).

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ethanrawson/bluelineR")
```

## A game

``` r

library(bluelineR)

nhl_scores("2026-10-20")[, c("id", "away_team_abbrev", "away_team_score", "home_team_abbrev", "home_team_score")]
#> # A tibble: 11 × 5
#>           id away_team_abbrev away_team_score home_team_abbrev home_team_score
#>        <int> <chr>                      <int> <chr>                      <int>
#> 1 2026020141 SJS                            4 MTL                            3
#> 2 2026020142 COL                            3 NJD                            4
#> 3 2026020143 ANA                            2 NYI                            3
#> 4 2026020144 LAK                            5 WSH                            2
#> 5 2026020145 TOR                            6 CBJ                            2
#> # ℹ 6 more rows
```

Play-by-play comes back one row per event, with the clock in seconds,
the strength, the players by name, the running score, and the location
turned so the shooting team always attacks to the right:

``` r

pbp <- nhl_pbp(2025020534)
pbp[pbp$type == "goal", c("period", "time_in_period", "event_team", "strength_state", "player_1_name", "x_fixed", "y_fixed")]
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   period time_in_period event_team strength_state player_1_name       x_fixed y_fixed
#>    <int> <chr>          <chr>      <chr>          <chr>                 <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1      1 13:38          EDM        5v4            Ryan Nugent-Hopkins      44      -6
#> 2      1 16:27          BOS        5v4            Pavel Zacha              82      -3
#> 3      2 14:38          EDM        5v5            Quinn Hutson             83       6
#> 4      3 01:41          EDM        4v5            Connor McDavid           87      -3
```

[`plot_shots()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/plot_shots.md)
puts each club at its own end, the away club at the left net:

``` r

plot_shots(pbp)
```

![Shot map of Edmonton at Boston: Edmonton at the left net, Boston at
the right.](reference/figures/README-shots-1.png)

## A goal, from the tracking

The NHL keeps about fourteen seconds of tracking behind every goal.
[`nhl_goal_tracking()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_goal_tracking.md)
fetches it (the files only answer requests that come from nhl.com, so it
says it does) as one row per skater, goalie and puck per frame, in feet:

``` r

frames <- nhl_goal_tracking(2025020534, 777)
frames
#> # A tibble: 1,683 × 9
#>   frame  time entity_id is_puck player_id sweater_number team      x       y
#>   <int> <dbl>     <dbl> <lgl>       <dbl>          <dbl> <chr> <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1     1     0         1 TRUE           NA             NA <NA>   77.9 -30.7  
#> 2     1     0      6001 FALSE     8480280              1 BOS   -87.3  -0.403
#> 3     1     0      6018 FALSE     8478401             18 BOS    81.0  -4.75 
#> 4     1     0      6028 FALSE     8477496             28 BOS    54.4  -0.288
#> 5     1     0      6039 FALSE     8479987             39 BOS    57.7  15.4  
#> # ℹ 1,678 more rows
```

[`classify_goal()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/classify_goal.md)
reads how it was scored. The same rules build the goal types on
BluelineMetrics, and the R port matches them goal for goal:

``` r

goal <- classify_goal(frames, team = "EDM", shot_type = "backhand")
goal[, c("shooter", "distance", "shot_speed", "since_neutral", "kinds")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   shooter distance shot_speed since_neutral kinds          
#>     <dbl>    <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl> <chr>          
#> 1 8478402      7.5       24.1           2.8 rush, breakaway
```

``` r

plot_goal(frames, title = "Connor McDavid, shorthanded breakaway at Boston, 18 Dec 2025")
```

![McDavid's shorthanded breakaway goal at Boston drawn from tracking:
every player's position as the puck goes in, with the last two seconds
of each path.](reference/figures/README-goal-1.png)

``` r

plot_goal_sequence(frames, n = 6, seconds = 5)
```

![Six frames leading up to the
goal.](reference/figures/README-sequence-1.png)

[`animate_goal()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/animate_goal.md)
plays it back as an MP4: every player and the puck, the scorer and his
assists named, his skating speed, and the last three seconds again at
half speed (it needs the [av](https://docs.ropensci.org/av/) package).

``` r

animate_goal(frames, "mcdavid.mp4", goal = nhl_goal_replay(2025020534, 777))
```

![McDavid's goal played back from the tracking: Boston's players in gold
and Edmonton's in navy move up the ice, McDavid's speed shows above him,
GOAL flashes as the puck goes in, and the last three seconds replay at
half speed.](reference/figures/README-animate.gif)

## Game tracking summaries

For 2021-22 to 2023-24 (and some of 2020-21 and 2024-25) the NHL’s
tracking vendor left a summary of every game: each player’s skating
speed, distance, zone time and zone starts, and **his puck possession
time**, in all, by zone and by strength, with each club’s possession
share. Individual possession is not in NHL EDGE.

``` r

tr <- nhl_tracking_summary(2023020500)
tr$teams[, c("team", "possession_pct", "possession_pct_o_zone", "possession_pct_d_zone")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   team  possession_pct possession_pct_o_zone possession_pct_d_zone
#>   <chr>          <dbl>                 <dbl>                 <dbl>
#> 1 FLA             51.5                  45.4                  34.4
#> 2 STL             48.5                  38.4                  42.0
top <- tr$players[order(-tr$players$possession_time), ]
top[, c("name", "team", "time_on_total", "possession_time", "possession_time_o_zone", "speed_max_mph", "distance_miles")]
#> # A tibble: 40 × 7
#>   name       team  time_on_total possession_time possession_time_o_zone speed_max_mph distance_miles
#>   <chr>      <chr>         <int>           <int>                  <int>         <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 Colton Pa… STL            1339              61                      5          20.7           3.28
#> 2 Brandon M… FLA            1704              57                     15          20.9           3.64
#> 3 Aaron Ekb… FLA             899              54                      8          20.2           3.27
#> 4 Jordan Ky… STL             960              48                     25          20.9           2.93
#> 5 Sam Reinh… FLA             759              45                     18          20.7           2.99
#> # ℹ 35 more rows
```

``` r
nhl_edge_leaders("skater_speed", season = "2025-26")[, c("rank", "player_first_name", "player_last_name", "player_team_abbrev", "max_speed_imperial", "bursts_over22")]

#>    rank player_first_name player_last_name player_team_abbrev max_speed_imperial bursts_over22

#> 2     2 Nathan            MacKinnon        COL                              24.8            45
#> 3     3 Connor            McDavid          EDM                              24.6           151
#> 4     4 Logan             Cooley           UTA                              24.4            33

mcdavid <- nhl_edge_skater(8478402, "2025-26")
mcdavid$info[, c("skating_speed_speed_max_imperial", "skating_speed_speed_max_percentile", "top_shot_speed_imperial", "total_distance_skated_imperial")]

#>   skating_speed_speed_max_imp…¹ skating_speed_speed_…² top_shot_speed_imper…³ total_distance_skate…⁴

```

## Best-on-best tournaments

Every tournament NHL players have played in: the Canada Cup, the World
Cup of Hockey, the Olympics and the 4 Nations Face-Off, from 1976 to
2026. Each player’s and club’s numbers at each one, careers with Olympic
medals, every game and every final. The game ids open the NHL’s
play-by-play, in full for the 4 Nations and the 2016 World Cup and goals
and penalties for the Olympics, and the 4 Nations goals have player
tracking:
`animate_goal(nhl_goal_tracking(2024200007, 1443), goal = nhl_goal_replay(2024200007, 1443))`
is McDavid’s overtime winner in the final.

``` r

oly <- nhl_international("skater", "olympics", 2026)
oly[, c("first_name", "last_name", "tri_code", "games_played", "goals", "assists", "points", "toi_seconds")]
#> # A tibble: 264 × 8
#>   first_name last_name  tri_code games_played goals assists points toi_seconds
#>   <chr>      <chr>      <chr>           <int> <int>   <int>  <int>       <int>
#> 1 Connor     McDavid    CAN                 6     2      11     13        7285
#> 2 Macklin    Celebrini  CAN                 6     5       5     10        7119
#> 3 Lucas      Raymond    SWE                 5     1       8      9        5560
#> 4 Joel       Armia      FIN                 6     3       5      8        4639
#> 5 Juraj      Slafkovský SVK                 6     4       4      8        7145
#> # ℹ 259 more rows

winners <- nhl_international_winners()
print(winners[, c("tournament", "year", "winning_tricode", "winning_score", "losing_tricode", "losing_score", "overtime")], n = 15)
#> # A tibble: 15 × 7
#>    tournament           year winning_tricode winning_score losing_tricode losing_score overtime
#>    <chr>               <dbl> <chr>                   <int> <chr>                 <int> <chr>   
#>  1 Canada Cup           1976 CAN                         5 TCH                       4 OT      
#>  2 Canada Cup           1981 URS                         8 CAN                       1 <NA>    
#>  3 Canada Cup           1984 CAN                         6 SWE                       5 <NA>    
#>  4 Canada Cup           1987 CAN                         6 URS                       5 <NA>    
#>  5 Canada Cup           1991 CAN                         4 USA                       2 <NA>    
#>  6 World Cup of Hockey  1996 USA                         5 CAN                       2 <NA>    
#>  7 Olympics             1998 CZE                         1 RUS                       0 <NA>    
#>  8 Olympics             2002 CAN                         5 USA                       2 <NA>    
#>  9 World Cup of Hockey  2004 CAN                         3 FIN                       2 <NA>    
#> 10 Olympics             2006 SWE                         3 FIN                       2 <NA>    
#> 11 Olympics             2010 CAN                         3 USA                       2 OT      
#> 12 Olympics             2014 CAN                         3 SWE                       0 <NA>    
#> 13 World Cup of Hockey  2016 CAN                         2 EUR                       1 <NA>    
#> 14 4 Nations Face-Off   2025 CAN                         3 USA                       2 OT      
#> 15 Olympics             2026 USA                         2 CAN                       1 OT

games <- nhl_international_games("4 nations")
final <- nhl_pbp(games$game_id[games$series_title == "Final"])
final[final$type == "goal", c("period", "time_in_period", "event_team", "player_1_name", "x_fixed", "y_fixed")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   period time_in_period event_team player_1_name    x_fixed y_fixed
#>    <int> <chr>          <chr>      <chr>              <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1      1 04:48          CAN        Nathan MacKinnon      41       7
#> 2      1 16:52          USA        Brady Tkachuk         80      -1
#> 3      2 07:32          USA        Jake Sanderson        73       7
#> 4      2 14:00          CAN        Sam Bennett           81      10
#> 5      4 08:18          CAN        Connor McDavid        68       6
```

## IIHF tournaments: every shot, located

The IIHF’s live-data feed has every game of its championships (the World
Championship, the World Juniors, the women’s and under-18 Worlds and the
divisions) and the 2026 Olympics, with every shot placed on the ice from
the 2019 tournaments on, goals and penalties, and each period’s team
stats. The 2026 Olympic final, Jack Hughes in overtime:

``` r

shots <- iihf_shots(1010000058)
shots[shots$result == "goal", c("period", "time", "team", "player_name", "x", "y", "distance")]
table(shots$team, shots$result)

wm <- iihf_schedule(2026, "wm")
wm[wm$phase %in% c("Semifinals", "BronzeMedalGame", "GoldMedalGame"), c("game_id", "date", "phase", "home_team", "away_team", "home_score", "away_score")]
#> # A tibble: 3 x 7
#>   period time  team  player_name     x     y distance
#>   <chr>  <chr> <chr> <chr>       <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 1      06:00 USA   Matt Boldy   80.8 -2.38     8.54
#> 2 2      38:16 CAN   Cale Makar   65.8 19.8     30.5 
#> 3 OT     61:41 USA   Jack Hughes  78   -3.57    11.6 
#>      
#>       blocked goal missed saved
#>   CAN      24    1     12    41
#>   USA      17    2     12    26
#> # A tibble: 4 x 7
#>   game_id date       phase           home_team away_team home_score away_score
#>   <chr>   <date>     <chr>           <chr>     <chr>          <int>      <int>
#> 1 12917   2026-05-30 Semifinals      SUI       NOR                6          0
#> 2 12918   2026-05-30 Semifinals      CAN       FIN                2          4
#> 3 12919   2026-05-31 BronzeMedalGame CAN       NOR                2          3
#> 4 12920   2026-05-31 GoldMedalGame   SUI       FIN                0          1
```

``` r

plot_shots(shots)
```

![Every shot of the 2026 Olympic final: USA at the left net, Canada at
the right; Hughes's overtime winner from the
slot.](reference/figures/README-iihf-1.png)

## DraftKings odds and player props

ESPN’s NHL odds come from DraftKings: every game’s moneyline, puck line
and total, opening and current, and DraftKings’ player props (shots,
points, assists, saves, goalscorer, milestones, club totals), each
over/under as one row with the no-vig chance and the player’s NHL id.

``` r

odds <- espn_odds()
odds[, c("home_team", "away_team", "home_ml", "away_ml", "home_win_prob", "total_line", "over_price", "under_price")]

props <- espn_props()
props[props$stat %in% "shots", c("team", "player_name", "player_id", "line", "over", "under", "over_prob")]
```

## Contracts, trades and coaches

The NHL’s APIs have no contract data, but Sportsnet publishes
PuckPedia’s tracker: every contract signed, with each season’s cap hit,
salary and bonuses, and every trade since 2020-21 with the cap hit and
the salary retained on each player moved. ESPN logs every roster move
and keeps the injury list, and the records site has every head coach and
general manager.

``` r

signings <- nhl_signings(2026)
signings[order(-signings$aav), c("player_name", "team", "contract_length", "aav", "signing_status", "clause")]
#> # A tibble: 618 × 6
#>   player_name       team  contract_length      aav signing_status clause
#>   <chr>             <chr>           <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>          <chr> 
#> 1 Cale Makar        COL                 8 20400000 UFA            NMC   
#> 2 Macklin Celebrini SJS                 5 18800000 RFA            <NA>  
#> 3 Leo Carlsson      ANA                 5 18000000 RFA            <NA>  
#> 4 Connor Bedard     CHI                 5 15000000 RFA            <NA>  
#> 5 Adam Fantilli     CBJ                 6 13750000 RFA            <NA>  
#> # ℹ 613 more rows

trades <- nhl_trades("2025-26", assets = TRUE)
retained <- trades[which(trades$retained_hit > 0), ]
retained[, c("trade_date", "team", "player_name", "cap_hit", "retained_hit")]
#> # A tibble: 14 × 5
#>   trade_date team  player_name        cap_hit retained_hit
#>   <date>     <chr> <chr>                <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1 2026-06-30 VGK   Parker Wotherspoon 1000000       500000
#> 2 2026-06-29 VAN   Brendan Gallagher  6500000      3250000
#> 3 2026-06-27 STL   Brandon Carlo      4100000       615000
#> 4 2026-06-25 FLA   Garnet Hathaway    2400000      1200000
#> 5 2026-03-06 LAK   Scott Laughton     3000000      1500000
#> # ℹ 9 more rows

nhl_coaches("team", active = TRUE)[, c("name", "team", "first_season", "games", "wins", "point_pctg")]
#> # A tibble: 32 × 6
#>   name            team  first_season games  wins point_pctg
#>   <chr>           <chr>        <int> <int> <int>      <dbl>
#> 1 Lindy Ruff      BUF       19971998  1339   661      0.561
#> 2 Jon Cooper      TBL       20122013  1052   629      0.640
#> 3 Jared Bednar    COL       20162017   792   450      0.616
#> 4 Rod Brind'Amour CAR       20182019   627   386      0.661
#> 5 Paul Maurice    FLA       20222023   338   186      0.586
#> # ℹ 27 more rows
```

## How far back it goes

Every season since 1917-18 is in the NHL’s data, but each kind of number
starts in its own year, and a column the league did not keep comes back
missing (or zero) before then.
[`nhl_stat_eras()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_stat_eras.md)
has the eras and, with `by = "stat"`, the first season of each stats
column, measured against the live API;
[`nhl_stats()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_stats.md),
[`nhl_pbp()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_pbp.md)
and
[`nhl_shifts()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_shifts.md)
say so when you ask for something older than the data.

| From | What starts |
|----|----|
| 1917-18 | Goals, assists, points, penalty minutes; goalie wins, goals against and shutouts; every game’s boxscore, player game logs, and play-by-play of goals and penalties |
| 1933-34 | Even-strength, power-play and short-handed goals and points |
| 1955-56 | Goalies’ shots against, saves and save percentage |
| 1959-60 | Shots and plus/minus |
| 1977-78 | Team power-play and penalty-kill percentages |
| 1997-98 | Ice time, shifts and faceoffs; shots on goal in the play-by-play |
| 2005-06 | Hits, blocked shots, giveaways, takeaways and missed shots |
| 2009-10 | Every event in the play-by-play, with its location (shot maps) |
| 2010-11 | Shift charts |
| 2021-22 | NHL EDGE tracking |
| 2023-24 | Goal tracking |

Gretzky’s 1981-82, from the league’s numbers and his game log: 92 goals,
and the fiftieth in his thirty-ninth game.

``` r

nhl_stats("skater/summary", "1981-82", sort = "points", limit = 5)[, c("skater_full_name", "team_abbrevs", "goals", "assists", "points")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   skater_full_name team_abbrevs goals assists points
#>   <chr>            <chr>        <int>   <int>  <int>
#> 1 Wayne Gretzky    EDM             92     120    212
#> 2 Mike Bossy       NYI             64      83    147
#> 3 Peter Stastny    QUE             46      93    139
#> 4 Dennis Maruk     WSH             60      76    136
#> 5 Bryan Trottier   NYI             50      79    129
log <- nhl_player_game_log(8447400, "1981-82")
log <- log[order(log$game_date), ]
fifty <- which(cumsum(log$goals) >= 50)[1]
fifty
#> [1] 39
log[fifty, c("game_date", "opponent_abbrev", "goals", "assists")]
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   game_date  opponent_abbrev goals assists
#>   <date>     <chr>           <int>   <int>
#> 1 1981-12-30 PHI                 5       1
```

[`nhl_era_adjust()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_era_adjust.md)
puts any seasons on one scale: each rescaled to the last ten seasons’
scoring, an 82-game schedule and today’s rosters (skaters dressed a
game), as Hockey-Reference adjusts. Howe’s 1952-53 and Gretzky’s
1981-82, side by side:

``` r

seasons <- rbind(nhl_stats("skater/summary", "1952-53", sort = "points", limit = 1),
                 nhl_stats("skater/summary", "1981-82", sort = "points", limit = 1))
nhl_era_adjust(seasons)[, c("skater_full_name", "season_id", "goals", "points", "adj_goals", "adj_points")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   skater_full_name season_id goals points adj_goals adj_points
#>   <chr>                <int> <int>  <int>     <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 Gordie Howe       19521953    49     95      59.7       122.
#> 2 Wayne Gretzky     19811982    92    212      66.2       155.
```

``` r
nhl_stats("skater/summary", "2025-26", sort = "points", limit = 5)[, c("skater_full_name", "team_abbrevs", "goals", "assists", "points")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   skater_full_name  team_abbrevs goals assists points

#> 2 Nikita Kucherov   TBL             44      86    130

```

## The records site

records.nhl.com keeps a century of tables.
[`nhl_records_catalog()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_records_catalog.md)
lists the 78 that answer, each with a line on what it holds, and helpers
cover the ones people ask for: Game 7, overtime, season-opener, outdoor
and overseas records, the draft lottery and its odds, and the milestones
in sight.

``` r

nhl_franchise_records("game7")[1:5, c("franchise_name", "games_played", "wins", "losses")]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>   franchise_name      games_played  wins losses
#>   <chr>                      <int> <int>  <int>
#> 1 Boston Bruins                 31    16     15
#> 2 Toronto Maple Leafs           28    12     16
#> 3 Montréal Canadiens            26    17      9
#> 4 Detroit Red Wings             25    14     11
#> 5 St. Louis Blues               19    10      9
nhl_draft_lottery(2026)[, c("draft_year", "pick", "lottery_team", "player_name", "effect")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   draft_year  pick lottery_team player_name   effect               
#>        <int> <int> <chr>        <chr>         <chr>                
#> 1       2026     1 TOR          Gavin McKenna Moved from 5th to 1st
#> 2       2026     2 SJS          Ivar Stenberg Moved from 9th to 2nd
```

## What it covers

| Area | Functions | Endpoint |
|----|----|----|
| Scores, schedule, standings | [`nhl_scores()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_scores.md), [`nhl_schedule()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_scores.md), [`nhl_team_schedule()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_scores.md), [`nhl_standings()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_standings.md) | `api-web.nhle.com/v1/score`, `/schedule`, `/club-schedule-season`, `/standings` |
| Games | [`nhl_pbp()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_pbp.md), [`nhl_boxscore()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_boxscore.md), [`nhl_game()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_game.md), [`nhl_shifts()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_shifts.md) | `/gamecenter/{id}/play-by-play`, `/boxscore`, `/landing`; `api.nhle.com/stats/rest/en/shiftcharts` |

## Being a good guest

These are the NHL’s own, undocumented APIs; bluelineR is not affiliated
with the NHL, and endpoints can change without notice. Requests are
throttled (five a second by default) and retried with backoff on rate
limits; turn on `options(bluelineR.cache = TRUE)` to keep responses for
the session.

Team and tournament logos and marks belong to their owners. bluelineR
doesn’t include any: it links to the NHL’s copies, which
`animate_goal(logos = TRUE)` downloads as it draws.

Contracts and trades come from Sportsnet’s stats API, which publishes
[PuckPedia](https://puckpedia.com)’s data; credit them when you use it.

bluelineR stands on the work of other R hockey packages, notably
[nhlscraper](https://rentosaijo.github.io/nhlscraper/),
[hockeyR](https://cran.r-project.org/package=hockeyR) and
[fastRhockey](https://cran.r-project.org/package=fastRhockey).
nhlscraper was first to the goal tracking frames: its `replay()` has
read them from `wsr.nhle.com` since November 2025, and `replays()`
serves a season of them at once. What bluelineR adds:

- **Contracts and trades**
  ([`nhl_signings()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_signings.md),
  [`nhl_trades()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_signings.md)):
  each contract’s cap hit, salary and bonuses season by season, and the
  salary retained in trades, from Sportsnet’s feed of PuckPedia’s data.
- **Game tracking summaries**
  ([`nhl_tracking_summary()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_tracking_summary.md)):
  each player’s puck possession time, by zone and strength, with speed,
  distance, zone time and zone starts, and each club’s possession share,
  from the per-game files at `live.nhle.com/ppt`.
- **Reading a goal from its tracking**
  ([`classify_goal()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/classify_goal.md)):
  rush, breakaway, odd-man rush, one-timer, cross-slot pass, traffic,
  behind the net and the forecheck, with who carried it in and who made
  the pass, and the frame the puck went in
  ([`goal_frame()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/goal_frame.md)).
- **Goal replays as video**
  ([`animate_goal()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/animate_goal.md)):
  the tracking played back on a rink as an MP4, with the scorer and his
  assists named, his skating speed and the finish again in slow motion.
- **Best-on-best tournaments**
  ([`nhl_international()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_international.md)
  and the rest): every Canada Cup, World Cup, Olympics and 4 Nations
  from records.nhl.com, with careers, Olympic medals, every game and
  every final.
- **IIHF tournaments with every shot located**
  ([`iihf_shots()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/iihf.md)
  and the rest): the World Championship, World Juniors, women’s and
  under-18 Worlds, the divisions and the 2026 Olympics, from the IIHF’s
  live-data feed, which no other package reads.
- **DraftKings player props**
  ([`espn_props()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/espn_odds.md)):
  ESPN’s prop list for every game, over and under paired and each player
  matched to his NHL id, with game lines
  ([`espn_odds()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/espn_odds.md))
  and
  [`devig()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/devig.md).
- **The newer NHL endpoints**: the v2 player bio with every award and
  its season
  ([`nhl_player_bio()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_player_bio.md)),
  the team comparison, the viewing guide, the quick standings and leader
  files, NHL.com news and videos, playoff series records and every
  playoff game, and all thirteen EDGE top-10 boards.
- **NHL EDGE** leaderboards, comparison reports and last night’s
  standouts, the goal replay summary
  ([`nhl_goal_replay()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_goal_tracking.md))
  and player search.

  [`nhl_seasons()`](https://ethanrawson.github.io/bluelineR/reference/nhl_teams.md)
